item.text: {"question_id":"5B.3","answer":"During 2023, the Tshisekedi administration had credible formal macro-fiscal safeguards: medium-term fiscal and debt planning, risk analysis, internal and budgetary controls, treasury and expenditure plans, audit arrangements, and publication requirements (BATCH-0029-E003; BATCH-0029-E005; BATCH-0017-E005). The administration also enacted or ratified measures concerning public debt, mining-royalty collection, carbon-credit revenue allocation, and banking of land and real-estate transactions (BATCH-0015-E009; BATCH-0015-E010; BATCH-0024-E006; BATCH-0015-E008). Tshisekedi personally directed fiscal, foreign-exchange, tax, and oversight bodies in July 2023 to stabilize the currency, prioritize spending, use normal expenditure procedures, and strengthen enforcement (BATCH-0024-E005). The central bank separately raised its policy rate and reported adherence to a no-monetary-financing pact, but those decisions are not directly attributable to Tshisekedi (BATCH-0023-E020). Evidence of administration and compliance is materially weaker: 2023 revenue realization was 91.22%, general-budget execution 87.38%, and central-government expenditure execution 96.49%, while end-period inflation reached 33.9% and annual-average inflation 23.33% (BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0024-E002). Parliamentary review, citing Court of Accounts observations, identified incoherent and emergency spending, weak provincial allocations, noncompliance with public-finance law, excessive overruns, uncertified debts, and works reported without observed field implementation (BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). Public financial scrutiny was further weakened by off-budget and special accounts, delayed or unpublished audits, ineffective anti-corruption enforcement, alleged phantom payroll payments, and official complicity in illicit mineral trade, although extractive-contract disclosure improved the EITI score (BATCH-0011-E013). Thus, the record supports formal rule enactment and some ruler-attributed corrective direction, but not reliable compliance or demonstrated protection of macroeconomic stability and long-term investment. Inflation, depreciation, and execution outcomes have multiple external and structural causes and cannot be assigned wholly to
